name: Memoria

paper.title: Memoria: Resolving Fateful Forgetting Problem through Human-Inspired Memory Architecture

construction.kept_as: learned compression of the previous segment's final hidden states
construction.processing: a trained attention abstractor with N_wm learnable queries turns segment t-1's last hidden states into N_wm engrams (working memory)
construction.writer: abstractor module inside the model, trained end to end with the task loss

organization.structure: three tiers (working, short-term queue, unbounded long-term) plus a directed weighted graph of co-retrieval counts over all engrams
organization.stores: working memory (this step's engrams), short-term memory (FIFO queue, fixed capacity), long-term memory (no size limit)
organization.index: squared L2 distance to working-memory engrams; co-retrieval count matrix as edge weights

management.operations: each step: co-retrieved pairs' counts +1; retrieved engrams gain lifespan in proportion to the memory attention they received; all engrams lose 1; WM moves to STM; STM overflow (oldest) moves to LTM
management.forgetting: lifespan decay: engrams whose lifespan reaches 0 are deleted permanently; only retrieval and use extend lifespan

retrieval.query: the current working-memory engrams (made from the previous segment)
retrieval.candidates: STM: top N_stm by mean exp(-L2^2) to WM; LTM: from each retrieved STM engram follow the strongest link into LTM, then walk the strongest unvisited links to depth 10
retrieval.selection: top N_ltm of the walked LTM engrams by similarity to WM
retrieval.budget: WM + STM + LTM engrams equal the segment length in sorting (1/8, 1/4, 5/8); 50/50/50 on Wikitext-103 and PG-19; 64/64/64 on Hyperpartisan

use.context: the model cross-attends to WM engrams and then to the retrieved STM/LTM engrams in every memory layer (same attention weights for both)
use.reasoning: one forward pass per segment; the memory attention weights are fed back as the lifespan increment

classify.note: STM candidates come from vector distance, but LTM is reached only by walking co-retrieval links from the retrieved STM engrams, which is the distinctive step.

stages.ingestion: The input is processed segment by segment (e.g. 150 tokens for Wikitext-103 and PG-19, 512 characters for enwik8, 256-1024 symbols for sorting).
stages.construction: A trained attention abstractor with N_wm learnable queries turns the previous segment's final hidden states (the current segment's layer-l states in the BERT variant) into N_wm engram vectors that form the working memory.
stages.organization: Engrams sit in working memory, a fixed-capacity short-term queue and an unbounded long-term store; every pair of engrams has a co-retrieval count, read as the directed edge weight Count_ij / Count_ii.
stages.update: After each step, co-retrieved engrams' pair counts rise by one (Hebbian), retrieved engrams gain lifespan proportional to the memory attention they received (scale α = 8), every engram loses 1, engrams at 0 are deleted, WM moves to STM and STM overflow moves to LTM.
stages.retrieval: Working memory is the cue: the N_stm STM engrams closest to it are retrieved; from each, the strongest link into LTM starts a greedy walk of depth 10 over unvisited LTM engrams, and the N_ltm walked engrams closest to WM are kept.
stages.answer: The model cross-attends to the WM engrams and then to the retrieved engrams inside its layers; the result is the next-token prediction (or class) for the current segment.
stages.learning: The abstractor and memory-attention layers are trained with the task loss (from scratch for language modeling and sorting, fine-tuned from BERT, RoBERTa or GPT-2 elsewhere); the memory rules themselves are fixed.

summary: Neural memory module with working, short-term and long-term stores of engram vectors, where Hebbian co-retrieval links guide search into long-term memory and a use-driven lifespan decides what is forgotten.
notes:
Architecture-level memory for Transformers, not an agent memory: engrams are latent vectors that the model attends to; there is no text store and no LLM prompting. Evaluated on synthetic sorting, language modeling (Wikitext-103, PG-19, enwik8) and Hyperpartisan classification.
VENUE: ICML 2024 (PMLR 235:39587-39615, proceedings.mlr.press/v235/park24a; OpenReview yTz0u4B8ug); the arXiv v3 PDF also carries the ICML 2024 footer.
DESIGN: §3.1-3.4, §4, App. D, E, G; code memoria.py and modeling_gpt2_with_memoria.py at v1.0.0 (the version the experiment requirements pin).

sources.code_note: Tag v1.0.0 (2023-10-06). The repo's experiment/requirements.txt pins memoria-pytorch==1.0.0, so this is the library version behind the experiments. Later commits (2024-09, v1.1.0) replaced exp(-L2^2) with -L2^2 in the similarity ("Prevent overflow of exp"), which changes the STM ranking because scores are averaged over WM engrams; the figures follow v1.0.0, which matches the paper.

sections.Details: App. D (hyperparameters), E (algorithms, complexity, Table 11), G (architectures)

abstract.text: Memoria is a memory module for neural networks that tries to keep important old information instead of always favouring the most recent input. It stores engram vectors in working, short-term and long-term memory, links engrams that are retrieved together (a Hebbian rule), searches long-term memory by following those links, and forgets engrams whose use-driven lifespan runs out. Plugged into GPT-2-style decoders and BERT/RoBERTa encoders, it beats Transformer-XL, Compressive Transformer and ∞-former on long sorting sequences and on language modeling, and improves long-document classification. An analysis of the surviving engrams shows primacy, recency and temporal-contiguity effects like those in human memory.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

headline: Memory holds vectors, not text: each engram is the abstractor's summary of a past segment, read through cross-attention.
Long-term memory is never searched by similarity alone: candidates are reached by walking co-retrieval links from the STM engrams, then ranked by distance to working memory.
Forgetting is driven by use: an engram lives only as long as it keeps receiving attention.

open_questions: The Full LTM Search variant (65.84) beats link-guided search (63.26) on 48K sorting, so the links trade accuracy for compute; no run isolates how much each saves in time.
Language-modeling gains over ∞-former are small on PG-19 (29.149 vs 29.154) and Memoria ties Compressive Transformer on enwik8 (1.16), and no variance is reported for these single runs.

text: A trained abstractor turns the previous segment's hidden states into a few engram vectors; they pass from working memory into a short-term queue and then into long-term memory.
Every step all engrams lose lifespan, those used by the model regain it, and engrams retrieved together are linked more strongly.

text: Working memory picks the nearest short-term engrams; their strongest links lead into long-term memory, which is walked 10 steps and ranked by distance to working memory (50 + 50 in the LM runs).
The model cross-attends to these engrams inside its layers, and the attention each receives becomes its new lifespan.

discussion.takeaway: Giving memory a use-driven lifespan and associative links lets a segment-recurrent Transformer keep information from the start of a very long sequence. The effect is clearest on long sorting sequences; language-modeling and classification gains are smaller.

claims.claim: Memoria resists fateful forgetting as sequences grow.
claims.evidence: Sorting with 32 segments of 1024: 63.42 vs 39.71 (∞-former), 35.07 (Compressive), 33.87 (Transformer-XL). Table 7, Fig. 4

claims.claim: Better language modeling than other memory Transformers.
claims.evidence: Wikitext-103 PPL 23.471 vs 24.543 Transformer-XL; PG-19 29.149 vs 29.154 ∞-former; enwik8 1.16 BPC tied with Compressive. Table 1
Hyperpartisan test F1 96.51 (Memoria RoBERTa) vs 95.24 RoBERTa, 94.56 Longformer, 93.24 BigBird. Table 2
LTM gain on 48K sorting falls from +8.39 to +1.26 with random wiring. Table 6

claims.claim: Memoria shows primacy, recency and temporal contiguity like human memory.
claims.evidence: Creation-time density of surviving engrams and link weight vs age difference on Wikitext-103. §6, Fig. 7

limits: The multi-store model it follows ignores the continuous levels-of-processing view of memory.
Interference, a main cause of forgetting in human long-term memory, is not modelled.
Memory built during inference may keep user data, which raises privacy concerns.
reading: Engrams are latent vectors read by cross-attention inside a trained model, so Memoria cannot be dropped into a frozen LLM or inspected as text; it is a different design point from agent memories.
The Hebbian search is a compute saving rather than an accuracy gain: exhaustive LTM search scores higher (65.84 vs 63.26, Table 6).
Wikitext-103, PG-19 and enwik8 numbers come from one run each; the PG-19 margin over ∞-former is 0.005 PPL.
Memoria BERT is below Longformer and BigBird on Hyperpartisan validation F1 (78.24 vs 78.33, 81.22); only the RoBERTa variant leads on both splits.
Hyperparameters differ by task (initial lifespan 5, 9 or 12; STM capacity 128 to 1,360), and Table 9 shows perplexity moving between 23.38 and 23.83 when they change.
